title: Daikin Furnace Code A01: Ignition Failure
meaning: The furnace failed to establish flame during the ignition sequence.
whenToCallPro: Ignitor or sensor service usually needed.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A01 means furnace failed to establish flame during the ignition sequence. Most often from worn ignitor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $150–$450.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A02: Flame Loss
meaning: Flame was lost during heating operation.
whenToCallPro: Professional inspection if flame loss repeats.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A02 means Flame was lost during heating operation. Most often from dirty sensor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $100–$400.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A03: Pressure Switch Open
meaning: The pressure switch did not close during venting.
whenToCallPro: Switch or inducer replacement may be needed.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A03 means pressure switch did not close during venting. Most often from blocked vent. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $175–$900.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A04: Limit Switch Open
meaning: The high-limit switch opened from overheating.
whenToCallPro: Limit or blower service if repeated.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A04 means high-limit switch opened from overheating. Most often from dirty filter. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $150–$600.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A05: Rollout Switch Open
meaning: The rollout switch tripped during burner operation.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the area and call a technician.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A05 means rollout switch tripped during burner operation. This is an emergency — do not attempt DIY repairs. Call a licensed technician immediately; typical repairs run $500–$3500.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A06: Gas Valve Fault
meaning: The control detected a gas valve circuit error.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A06 means control detected a gas valve circuit error. This is an emergency — do not attempt DIY repairs. Call a licensed technician immediately; typical repairs run $350–$900.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A07: Blower Motor Fault
meaning: The blower motor did not start or tripped.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A07 means blower motor did not start or tripped. Most often from failed motor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $450–$1200.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A08: Inducer Motor Fault
meaning: The inducer motor failed during venting.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A08 means inducer motor failed during venting. Most often from seized inducer. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $400–$900.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A09: Control Board Fault
meaning: The control board reported an internal error.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A09 means control board reported an internal error. Most often from surge damage. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $300–$800.

title: Daikin Furnace Code A10: Condensate Fault
meaning: A condensate drainage fault triggered lockout on high-efficiency models.
whenToCallPro: Replace pump or switch if drainage is clear.
snippetAnswer: Daikin furnace code A10 means A condensate drainage fault triggered lockout on high-efficiency models. Often caused by clogged trap. Usually safe to try basic checks yourself; professional repairs run $150–$450.
